description: EAGLE editor commands from EXPORT to MOVE in the order of the built-in help: exporting netlists, part and pin lists, library scripts and images, fan-out of SMD/BGA devices, drawing frames, grid and units, groups, holes, object properties, gate invocation, junctions and labels, layers, lines and arcs, locking, marks, meanders, custom command menus, mirror, miter, hierarchical modules and moving objects. Each command can be typed in the editor command line, assigned to a key or written into a .scr script; coordinates are (x y) in the current GRID unit, '•' in the syntax stands for a mouse click, and ';' ends a command that has fewer than its maximum number of parameters.

tools.name: EXPORT
tools.description: Writes data files from the drawing or library that is open: a library as script, netlists (EAGLE and SPICE format), a netlist script, part and pin lists, a library directory, or an image of the drawing. Output goes to the project directory by default. Use it to pass data to other programs; many more formats (DXF, Hyperlynx and others) are produced by ULPs started with RUN, several of them listed under File > Export.

parameters.name: SCRIPT
parameters.description: Library opened with OPEN as a script file (see 'EXPORT SCRIPT').

parameters.name: NETLIST
parameters.description: ASCII netlist of schematic or board (see 'EXPORT NETLIST').

parameters.name: SPICENETLIST
parameters.description: SPICE-format netlist of the loaded schematic, only nets connected to elements (see EXPORT SPICENETLIST in the SPICE simulation category).

parameters.name: NETSCRIPT
parameters.description: Schematic netlist as a script for boards.

parameters.name: PARTLIST
parameters.description: Component list of schematic or board.

parameters.name: PINLIST
parameters.description: Pads/pins with pin directions and connected nets.

parameters.name: DIRECTORY
parameters.description: Directory (contents list) of the currently opened library.

parameters.name: IMAGE
parameters.description: Bitmap image of the drawing or the clipboard (see 'EXPORT IMAGE').

tools.notes: Relative file names are written to the project directory. For 3D data use the separate EXPORTSTEP command; for Gerber and drill data use the CAM Processor. The editor needs a working sign-in since the June 2026 licensing shutdown, so for headless jobs prefer reading the XML design files or eaglecon's CAM mode.

tools.name: EXPORT NETLIST
tools.description: Writes an ASCII netlist of the loaded schematic or board. Only nets that are connected to elements are listed. Use it for cross-checking connectivity, test fixtures or import into other tools.
tools.notes: For a SPICE netlist use EXPORT SPICENETLIST; to carry connectivity into a board use EXPORT NETSCRIPT; for a list of every pin with its direction use EXPORT PINLIST.

tools.name: EXPORT NETSCRIPT
tools.description: Writes the netlist of the loaded schematic as an EAGLE script file. Running that script in a board whose elements are already placed (or whose signals were removed with DELETE SIGNALS) reads in the new or changed connections. This is the classic way to update a board's connectivity without forward/back annotation.
tools.notes: While the script is read into a board, no schematic that is consistent with this board may be loaded. Related: DELETE SIGNALS, SCRIPT.

tools.name: EXPORT PARTLIST
tools.description: Writes a component list of the loaded schematic or board. Only elements that have pins or pads are included, so pin-less devices such as frames do not appear. Use it for a quick bill of materials.
tools.notes: For a configurable bill of materials (attributes, other file formats) run a BOM ULP such as bom.ulp with RUN.

tools.name: EXPORT PINLIST
tools.description: Writes a list of the pads and pins of the drawing with their pin directions and the names of the nets connected to them. Useful for reviewing pin assignments of large ICs or for connector documentation.
tools.notes: Pin directions are those defined in the symbols (CHANGE DIRECTION / PIN).

tools.name: EXPORT SCRIPT
tools.description: Writes a library that was opened with OPEN as a script of editor commands, which can be edited as text and read back with SCRIPT. Use it for bulk changes, version control of libraries or to rebuild a library.
tools.notes: Import into a new, empty library, otherwise objects get defined twice. SET UNDO_LOG OFF before reading speeds up the script. OPEN with an unknown name creates a new library in the first directory of the library path.

tools.name: EXPORT DIRECTORY
tools.description: Writes the directory (list of contents) of the library currently opened with OPEN to a text file. Handy for documenting what a library contains.
tools.notes: In the library editor EDIT; shows the library's table of contents interactively.

tools.name: EXPORT IMAGE
tools.description: Writes an image of the current drawing (schematic, board or library object) at a given resolution; the file extension selects the format. It can also copy the image to the system clipboard, produce black and white output, or capture only the visible window area.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Extension chooses the format: .bmp, .png, .pbm, .pgm, .ppm, .tif, .xbm, .xpm.

parameters.name: CLIPBOARD
parameters.description: Copy the image to the system clipboard instead of a file (case does not matter).

parameters.name: MONOCHROME
parameters.description: Black and white image.

parameters.name: WINDOW
parameters.description: Only the area currently visible in the editor window; without it the whole drawing.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Resolution in dpi.

tools.notes: Choose the visible layers with DISPLAY first to control what appears; DISPLAY LAST restores the previous set. High resolutions of large boards produce very large bitmaps.

tools.name: FANOUT
tools.description: Board command that creates short routed wires with vias (fan-outs) from the pads of an SMD or BGA device, or from all pads of a signal, so that inner layers can be reached. Through-hole pads are ignored. Wire width and via drill/diameter come from the current settings, and fan-outs that would break the design rules are skipped.
tools.usage:
FANOUT DEVICE device-name [direction]
FANOUT SIGNAL signal-name [direction]

parameters.name: DEVICE device-name
parameters.description: Fan out all SMD pads of this element.

parameters.name: SIGNAL signal-name
parameters.description: Fan out the pads belonging to this signal.

parameters.name: OUT
parameters.description: Fan-outs go away from the device center.

parameters.name: IN
parameters.description: Fan-outs go toward the device center.

parameters.name: ALTERNATE
parameters.description: Alternate OUT and IN for adjacent pads; helps where space is tight.

parameters.name: Allow Violations (toolbar)
parameters.description: Create vias even if they violate the rules against a neighbouring fan-out, to see why a via is missing (default off).

tools.notes: Width and drill below the design-rule minimum are raised to the minimum. The distance from pad to via follows the same-signal 'Smd To Via' clearance in the design rules. If fan-outs are missing, check width, drill and the net class minimums. Left click selects the device or signal interactively. Related: AUTO BGA, ROUTE, CHANGE.

tools.name: FILTER
tools.description: Runs a selection filter from the command line, either a saved filter by name or a filter expression given as a string. Filters (Design Manager > Filters tab) select objects dynamically by type, properties, memberships and attributes, e.g. all resistors in an 0603 footprint, in schematics and boards.

parameters.name: G
parameters.description: Load the filter from the EAGLE settings (global); without G it is a local filter saved in the design.

parameters.name: filter-name
parameters.description: Name of the saved filter.

parameters.name: '<expression>'
parameters.description: Filter expression such as ((ObjectType = Part) AND (Name = R*)); every criterion in parentheses, combined with AND/OR, '!' negates.

tools.example:
FILTER RUN '((ObjectType = Part) AND (Name = R*) AND (HasFootprint 0603))'
FILTER RUN G LockedParts
tools.notes: Criteria include ObjectType, Name, Value, DeviceName, Width, Rotation, IsLocked, IsMirrored, InNetClass, InLibrary, OnLayer, InNet, OnSignal, OnSheet, HasAttribute, HasFootprint, HasPin and more; some apply only to SCH or BRD. See the Filters Tab help topic for the full list.

tools.name: FRAME
tools.description: Draws a drawing frame with numbered columns and lettered rows between two corner points, in schematics, boards or (more typically) in a frame symbol or footprint that also contains a title block. The first frame in a drawing is used to compute part and net positions for cross-reference labels and ULPs.

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: Number of columns, up to 127, numbered left to right; a negative value numbers them right to left.

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: Number of rows, up to 26, lettered from A top to bottom; negative = bottom to top. Requires columns before it.

parameters.name: borders
parameters.description: Which sides carry the number/letter border: LEFT, TOP, RIGHT, BOTTOM, or NONE / ALL (default: all four).

tools.notes: Center mouse button changes the layer. A frame has no rotation of its own and is not rotated by ROTATE. Only the first frame counts for positions. Existing frames are changed with CHANGE COLUMS / ROWS / BORDER. The 'frames' library shipped with EAGLE contains ready-made frames.

tools.name: GATESWAP
tools.description: Swaps two equivalent gates in a schematic, e.g. two NAND gates, to simplify board routing. Both gates must be identical with the same number of pins and the same swaplevel (greater than 0) from the device definition; they may belong to different parts.

parameters.name: gate_name
parameters.description: Displayed gate name in the schematic, e.g. U1A for gate A of U1.

tools.notes: A part that has no gates left in use after the swap is deleted automatically. Related: PINSWAP, ADD (swaplevel), CHANGE SWAPLEVEL.

tools.name: GRID
tools.description: Sets the grid spacing, grid display and the unit used for coordinates and values in all editors. Without options it toggles the grid display (also F6). Every script should set the grid unit first because all following coordinates and sizes are read in that unit.

parameters.name: ON | OFF
parameters.description: Show or hide the grid.

parameters.name: DOTS | LINES
parameters.description: Grid shown as dots or solid lines.

parameters.name: MIC | MM | MIL | INCH
parameters.description: Grid unit.

parameters.name: FINEST
parameters.description: Finest possible grid.

parameters.name: grid_size [grid_multiple]
parameters.description: Grid distance in the current unit; the optional second number shows only every n-th grid line.

parameters.name: LAST
parameters.description: Return to the previous grid settings.

parameters.name: DEFAULT
parameters.description: Standard grid for the current drawing type.

parameters.name: ALT ...
parameters.description: Alternate grid, active while Alt is held (see 'GRID units and alt grid').

tools.notes: The first number is always the distance, the second the multiple. A unit after the size (GRID inch 0.05 mm) sets the display unit of the cursor coordinates. GRID LAST restores whatever was set before, so scripts can change the grid temporarily. Parameter aliases: see 'GRID parameter aliases'.

tools.name: GRID units and alt grid
tools.description: The GRID unit keywords choose micron, millimeter, mil or inch; a second unit after the grid size changes only the unit in which cursor coordinates are displayed. GRID ALT defines an alternate, usually finer, grid that is active only while the Alt key is held, for fine positioning in dense areas.

parameters.name: unit grid_size unit
parameters.description: E.g. GRID inch 0.05 mm: 0.05 inch grid, coordinates displayed in mm.

parameters.name: ALT unit grid_size [unit]
parameters.description: Alternate grid, e.g. alt mm 1 mil: 1 mm alternate grid displayed in mil.

tools.example:
GRID mil 50 2 lines on alt mm 1 mil;
GRID inch 0.05 mm;
tools.notes: In coordinates a unit may be appended independently of the grid, e.g. (100mil 200mil); allowed units are mm, mic, mil and in, and x and y may differ. Polar (P) and relative (R) coordinate modifiers refer to the MARK.

tools.name: GRID parameter aliases
tools.description: Parameter aliases store a GRID setting under a name, so frequently used grids (e.g. a fine SMD grid and a coarse placement grid) can be recalled with one short command. The aliases also pop up when the GRID button is held down or right-clicked.
tools.usage:
GRID = name parameters
GRID = name @
GRID = ?
GRID = name
GRID = name;
GRID name

parameters.name: = name parameters
parameters.description: Define the alias; name has letters, digits and underscores, starts with a letter or underscore, is case-insensitive and must not be an option keyword.

parameters.name: = name @
parameters.description: Define the alias from the current grid settings.
Ask for a name for the current settings.

parameters.name: = name
parameters.description: Open the GRID dialog to set the grid for this alias.

parameters.name: = name;
parameters.description: Delete the alias.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Apply the alias; may be abbreviated and combined with other parameters (aliases win over keywords when abbreviated).

tools.notes: DISPLAY supports the same alias mechanism for layer sets.

tools.name: GROUP
tools.description: Defines a temporary group of objects for a following command such as MOVE, CHANGE, DELETE, MIRROR, ROTATE, COPY or CUT (applied with a Ctrl+right click). Objects are selected by dragging a rectangle or clicking a polygon; GROUP ALL takes the whole drawing. Only objects on visible layers become members.

parameters.description: Polygon corners; close it with a right click or by returning to the first point.

parameters.name: ALL
parameters.description: Group the entire drawing area (Ctrl+A).
GROUP; clears the group definition.

tools.notes: Mouse: Left&Drag = rectangle, Shift+click adds to the existing group, Ctrl+Left toggles one object, Ctrl+Shift+Left toggles the higher-level object (e.g. a whole net segment), Right closes the polygon. Membership: objects with their origin inside, wires with at least one end inside (only that end moves), circles with center inside, rectangles with any corner inside. The group lasts until another drawing is loaded or GROUP; is given. The Enable Attribute Selection toolbar toggle controls whether attributes are selected. With Options/Set/Misc 'Group default on', selection is the default mode (Esc clears, drag moves, Backspace deletes). Named persistent groups are made with NEWGROUP/EDITGROUP.

tools.name: HELP
tools.description: Opens the context-sensitive help window, or the help page of a given command. F1 opens help for the active command.
tools.notes: The help pages are the authoritative reference for the command syntax used in scripts.

tools.name: HOLE
tools.description: Places non-plated drill holes (mounting holes) in a board or footprint; they have no electrical connection between layers. The drill diameter is given in the current unit and stays as the preset for later holes, vias and pads.

parameters.name: drill
parameters.description: Hole diameter in the current unit, up to 200 mm.

tools.notes: A hole creates a drill symbol in the Holes layer (45) and a circle in the Dimension layer (20), so the autorouter keeps its board-edge distance from it; tStop/bStop get a solder-mask opening sized by the design rules. Holes can only be selected when the Holes layer is visible. Change the diameter with CHANGE DRILL value •. Drill symbols are assigned in Options/Set/Drill. Related: VIA, PAD.

tools.name: INFO
tools.description: Shows the properties of an object (layer, width, size, position, attributes...) in a dialog where they can also be modified. Objects can be clicked or selected by name, which reaches parts outside the visible window area.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Part, pad, SMD, pin or gate name; multi-gate parts need the full instance name (IC1A); part attributes as R5>VALUE.

tools.notes: The coordinates of a rotated rectangle cannot be changed. In design-block editing mode INFO .dbl edits the design block's description and attributes. The Enable Attribute Selection toolbar toggle controls whether attributes can be picked. Related: CHANGE, SHOW.

tools.name: INVOKE
tools.description: Schematic command that places a particular gate of a part that already exists, for example the power gate of a logic IC (addlevel REQUEST), a CAN gate, or an ALWAYS gate that was deleted. Give the part name (and gate) or click an existing gate, choose the gate in the popup, then click to place it.
tools.usage:
INVOKE • orientation •
INVOKE part_name gate_name orientation •

parameters.name: part_name
parameters.description: Existing part, e.g. IC5; needed when the gate goes onto another sheet than the part's other gates.

parameters.name: gate_name
parameters.description: Gate to place, e.g. PWR.

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: R0, R90, MR0 ... as in ADD.

tools.notes: Mouse: center button mirrors, right rotates, Shift+Right rotates back. In the dialog the right column shows on which sheets gates are already placed; selecting an already invoked gate turns the button into 'Show', which zooms to it. Use INVOKE instead of COPY to get another gate of the same part.

tools.name: JUNCTION
tools.description: Places a connection dot on a schematic net where wires meet and are connected. If placed at a crossing of different nets, you are asked whether to connect them. Junctions are added automatically where a net wire ends on a point with at least two other net wires or pins.
tools.notes: Automatic junctions can be turned off with SET AUTO_JUNCTION OFF; or Options/Set/Misc 'Auto set junction'. Junctions can only be placed on a net. Related: NET.

tools.name: LABEL
tools.description: Places a text label showing the name of a net or bus in a schematic: click the net or bus, then click where the label goes. Labels always show the current name (they follow renames with NAME) and a net may have any number of them; with XREF the label becomes a cross-reference label pointing to the next sheet where the net appears.

parameters.name: XREF
parameters.description: Create a cross-reference label (see 'LABEL XREF (cross-reference labels)').

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: R0, R90, R180, R270 etc. as in ADD.

tools.notes: Mouse: center button selects the layer, right rotates, Shift+Right rotates back. Labels cannot be edited with CHANGE TEXT. SHOW on a net, bus or label highlights all connected ones. LABEL keeps its own layer: in a script select it while LABEL is active (LABEL parameters, newline LAYER layer, newline more parameters;) rather than with a LAYER command before it. Related: NAME, BUS, FRAME.

tools.name: LABEL XREF (cross-reference labels)
tools.description: Cross-reference labels show, in multi-sheet schematics, on which other sheet (and in which frame field) a net continues, e.g. VCC/3.4B with the default format. The label orientation decides whether it points to a higher sheet (R0, R270) or a lower one (R90, R180). They work for nets only, not busses.

parameters.name: %F
parameters.description: Draw a flag border around the label.

parameters.name: %N
parameters.description: Net name.

parameters.name: %S
parameters.description: Number of the next sheet.

parameters.name: %C / %R
parameters.description: Column / row on that sheet (needs a FRAME there, otherwise '?').

parameters.name: default format
parameters.description: %F%N/%S.%C%R; other ASCII characters may be added.

tools.notes: If the net appears only on the current sheet only its name is shown; if there is no sheet in the pointing direction the other direction is used. An XREF label placed on a net wire end connects to it and moves with it. The format string is stored in the schematic; it can also be set in Options/Set/Misc. The parameter toolbar Xref button and CHANGE XREF switch between normal and cross-reference labels.

tools.name: LAUNCH
tools.description: Opens Autodesk's web-based 3D package generator or 3D package search from the library editor. In the device editor it creates a new device variant (like PACKAGE); in the library editor it imports a package into the library (like COPY).

parameters.name: PACKAGE3D-GENERATOR [managed_folder_id]
parameters.description: Start the generator; the optional managed folder receives the new asset (otherwise a folder selection dialog may appear for local libraries with write access to several hubs).

parameters.name: PACKAGE3D-WEB-SEARCH
parameters.description: Search existing 3D packages on the web.

tools.notes: Relies on Autodesk online services and managed folders (hubs), i.e. a signed-in, online session; not usable in offline automation. 3D packages created for a managed library go into that library's managed folder by default.

tools.name: LAYER
tools.description: Selects the current drawing layer (with one parameter), defines a new layer or renames one (number and name), or deletes an empty user layer (minus sign). Available in all editors; from the menu it shows a popup of the available layers.
tools.usage:
LAYER layer_number
LAYER layer_name
LAYER layer_number layer_name
LAYER [??] -layer_number

parameters.name: layer_number | layer_name
parameters.description: Make this the current layer for LINE, CIRCLE, RECT, POLYGON, TEXT etc.

parameters.name: layer_number layer_name
parameters.description: Define a new layer or rename one; use numbers above 100 for own layers. Pairs 53/54, 55/56, 57/58, 59/60 may be defined as top/bottom pairs that swap with MIRROR.

parameters.name: -layer_number
parameters.description: Delete the layer; it must be empty ('layer is not empty: #').
Suppress error messages when deleting (layer not empty or not present), useful in scripts.

tools.notes: Only signal layers entered in the design-rules layer setup are available. Predefined layers can be renamed but keep their function. Layers used by a footprint are added to the board when it is placed. ATTRIBUTE and LABEL keep their own layer and ignore a preceding LAYER command. Layer presets (eagle.scr predefined, up to 9 user-defined per editor type) are managed in the layer dialog; a preset named like a layer (e.g. 'top') overrides that name in DISPLAY. See 'Predefined layers' for the numbers.

tools.name: Predefined layers
tools.description: The fixed layer numbers of EAGLE, used by LAYER, DISPLAY, CHANGE LAYER, CAM jobs and the XML files. Board layers are 1..52, schematic layers 91..98 plus 100 and 101; the numbers keep their function even when a layer is renamed.

parameters.name: 1 Top, 2..15 Route2..Route15, 16 Bottom
parameters.description: Copper layers (tracks); only those in the layer setup are usable.

parameters.name: 17 Pads, 18 Vias
parameters.description: Through-hole pads and vias.

parameters.name: 19 Unrouted
parameters.description: Airwires (rubberbands).

parameters.name: 20 Dimension
parameters.description: Board outline and circles of holes; limits the autorouter.

parameters.name: 21 tPlace, 22 bPlace
parameters.description: Silkscreen top/bottom.

parameters.name: 23 tOrigins, 24 bOrigins
parameters.description: Element origins; must be visible to select elements.

parameters.name: 25 tNames, 26 bNames / 27 tValues, 28 bValues
parameters.description: Component names (service print) and values.

parameters.name: 29 tStop, 30 bStop / 31 tCream, 32 bCream
parameters.description: Solder stop mask and solder cream (paste).

parameters.name: 33 tFinish, 34 bFinish / 35 tGlue, 36 bGlue / 37 tTest, 38 bTest
parameters.description: Finish, glue mask, test and adjustment information.

parameters.name: 39 tKeepout, 40 bKeepout
parameters.description: No-go areas for components.

parameters.name: 41 tRestrict, 42 bRestrict, 43 vRestrict
parameters.description: No-go areas for tracks (top/bottom) and vias.

parameters.name: 44 Drills, 45 Holes
parameters.description: Plated (conducting) and non-plated drill holes.

parameters.name: 46 Milling, 47 Measures, 48 Document, 49 Reference
parameters.description: Milling contours, measures, general documentation, reference marks.

parameters.name: 51 tDocu, 52 bDocu
parameters.description: Part documentation top/bottom.

parameters.name: 91 Nets, 92 Busses, 93 Pins, 94 Symbols, 95 Names, 96 Values, 97 Info, 98 Guide
parameters.description: Schematic layers.

parameters.name: 100 SimOp, 101 SimProbes
parameters.description: Schematic simulation layers: operating-point results and result probes.

tools.notes: Top/bottom pairs (tPlace/bPlace etc.) swap when an element is mirrored. User layers should use numbers above 100 (in schematics 100 and 101 are taken by the simulator).

tools.name: LINE
tools.description: Draws lines (plain wires) and, in copper layers, routed tracks: each click adds a segment, two clicks at the same point end the line. It is also the general way to draw board outlines in the Dimension layer and graphics in symbols and footprints. Formerly called WIRE (the keyword is deprecated).

parameters.name: 'signal_name'
parameters.description: Add all following lines as wires of this signal without automatic checks; for script-imported data. Run DRC afterwards (shorts possible).

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Line width in the current unit, up to 200 mm; preset/changed with CHANGE WIDTH.

parameters.name: ROUND | FLAT
parameters.description: End caps for arcs (straight lines always have round ends).

parameters.name: curve | @radius
parameters.description: Draw an arc segment (see 'LINE arcs (curve and @radius)').

tools.notes: Mouse: center button selects the layer, right changes the bend style (SET Wire_Bend; Shift+Right reverses, Ctrl+Right toggles corresponding styles), Ctrl+Left at the start snaps to the nearest existing line end and adopts its width, layer and style, Ctrl+Left at an end point sets an arc radius. Lines in Top, Bottom and Route2..15 are signal wires: starting on an existing signal joins it, ending on another signal asks whether to connect. Each segment is a separate object. Styles Continuous, LongDash, ShortDash, DashDot (CHANGE STYLE) are for drawings only; DRC treats all lines as continuous. Prefer NET, BUS, SIGNAL and ROUTE for connections. Related: ARC, MITER, SPLIT, RIPUP.

tools.name: LINE arcs (curve and @radius)
tools.description: LINE can draw arc segments directly: a signed curve value gives the arc angle, a signed @radius gives its radius. This is the main way scripts generate arcs, round board corners and curved tracks; ROUND/FLAT choose the end caps of the arc.

parameters.name: curve
parameters.description: Angle of the arc in degrees, range -360 < curve < +360 (exclusive); positive = counterclockwise. Must always carry a sign ('+90') to distinguish it from the width; 0 is a straight line.

parameters.name: @radius
parameters.description: Arc radius with sign for the direction (@+100 counterclockwise). If the end point is more than twice the radius away, a straight line results.

parameters.name: ROUND | FLAT
parameters.description: Arc end caps; default ROUND.

tools.notes: Full circles cannot be drawn this way; use CIRCLE. Interactively, placing an end point with Ctrl sets the radius, and Ctrl+Right toggles the arc orientation. MOVE with Ctrl on the middle of a wire bends it into an arc.

tools.name: LOCK
tools.description: Board command that locks parts, wires, vias, polygons and holes so they cannot be moved, rotated or mirrored, e.g. connectors and mounting holes at fixed positions. It can lock objects by click, by name, all at once, or all objects of a layer, and the minus forms unlock them.

parameters.description: Lock / unlock all objects.

parameters.name: name / -name
parameters.description: Lock / unlock the named element.

parameters.name: LAYER [-]layer
parameters.description: Lock / unlock all objects in a layer, by name or number.

tools.notes: Mouse: Shift+Left unlocks, Ctrl+Right applies to the group, Ctrl+Shift+Right unlocks all locked objects in the group; the toolbar offers lock all / unlock all / lock active layer. A locked part shows its origin as 'X', locked wires, vias and holes a padlock. Locked objects stay in place when a group is moved; detached texts of a locked part can still be moved individually. Related: MOVE, MIRROR, ROTATE, REPOSITION.

tools.name: MARK
tools.description: Sets a reference point in the drawing; the cursor position relative to it is then shown at the top left of the window with a leading 'R'. Used to measure distances and to enter relative (R) and polar (P) coordinates in scripts. MARK; switches the mark on or off.
tools.notes: Choose a fine enough grid before setting the mark. Without a mark, R and P coordinates are relative to the drawing origin; P means (radius angle) with the angle counterclockwise in degrees.

tools.name: MEANDER
tools.description: Board command that adds meander (serpentine) segments to a routed signal to equalise the lengths of a differential pair or to lengthen any signal to a target length. Click a wire and move the cursor away; the distance sets the meander amplitude and an indicator shows the target length and the deviation in percent.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Target length (current unit); may be typed at any time. 0 resets it. For a differential pair the two segments are balanced first, then both are lengthened.

tools.notes: Mouse: Ctrl+Left measures the length of the clicked segment (use it as target for another), Ctrl+Shift+Left takes the maximum of the segments measured so far (bus length matching), Right toggles symmetrical/asymmetrical meanders. Several meanders can be added at different places. The deviation shows green within the design-rule 'Misc/Max. length difference in differential pairs' (default 10mm), red otherwise. Related: ROUTE, ROUTEDIFF.

tools.name: MENU
tools.description: Replaces the text command menu with a user-defined list of buttons, which may run single commands, command sequences under a short label, or open submenus, optionally with icons. MENU; restores the default menu. Put the definition into a script such as eagle.scr (run when an editor opens) to keep it.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: A command name used as both label and command (MENU Display Grid;).

parameters.name: 'label : commands;'
parameters.description: Label with the commands executed behind the colon.
The semicolon button, used to terminate many commands; always include it.
Delimiter for grouping buttons.

tools.example:
MENU Move Delete Rotate Route ';' Edit;
MENU;
tools.notes: Options with more than one word or that could be read as a command must be in single quotes. For submenus and icons see 'MENU submenus and icons'. To put a MENU on a key with ASSIGN, write its ';' as three pairs of apostrophes.

tools.name: MENU submenus and icons
tools.description: The full MENU grammar allows aliased commands (label : commands), submenus in braces with '|' separated entries, delimiters and icons given as [filename]. With an icon a top-level button shows only the icon and uses the text as tooltip; in popup menus both are shown.
tools.usage:
option    := command | submenu | delimiter
command   := [ icon ] text1 [ ':' text2 ]
submenu   := [ icon ] text '{' option [ '|' option ] '}'
icon      := '[' filename ']'
delimiter := '---'

parameters.name: text1 : text2
parameters.description: Button label and the command sequence it runs.
Submenu; '|' separates its entries.

parameters.name: [filename]
parameters.description: Icon file; without a path it is searched in the working directory and EAGLE's bin directory. No extra quoting needed for spaces.

tools.notes: Spread long definitions over several lines by ending each line with a backslash. Submenus may be nested (e.g. Draw > Wire > DashDot : CHANGE STYLE DashDot; LINE).

tools.name: MIRROR
tools.description: Mirrors objects about the y axis; in a board this moves components to the bottom side, together with their connected wires on the outer layers. Objects can be clicked or selected by name, and a group is mirrored with Ctrl+right click.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Part, pad, SMD or pin name; part attributes as R5>VALUE.

tools.notes: Elements can only be mirrored with tOrigins/bOrigins visible and not when locked. Connected outer-layer wires are mirrored too (check for shorts); objects on inner layers and vias keep their layer. Wires, circles, pads and polygons can be mirrored only as part of a group, which is mirrored about the vertical axis through the next grid point. Texts on the bottom side are mirrored automatically to read correctly from below; mirrored schematic text stays readable. Related: ROTATE, LOCK, TEXT.

tools.name: MITER
tools.description: Rounds or chamfers the joint of two wires by inserting an arc (positive radius) or a straight segment (negative radius). Click the joint of exactly two straight wires, or a wire between two straight wires to re-miter it. The radius also sets the automatic mitering of other wire-drawing commands in 90 and 45 degree bend styles.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: Positive = arc of that radius, negative = straight chamfer (the '-' reads as 'straight').

tools.notes: Both wires must be on the same layer with the same width and style. Left&Drag adjusts the miter dynamically; Right toggles round/straight. Round mitering applies to both 90 and 45 degree bend styles, straight mitering only to the 90 degree styles. Related: SPLIT, LINE, ROUTE.

tools.name: MODULE
tools.description: Creates modules for hierarchical schematics and places module instances on a sheet. A module is a sub-schematic with ports (PORT); each instance adds the module's parts and nets to the board, with names derived from the instance name or an offset. Instances can also be placed inside modules for deeper hierarchies.

parameters.name: width height
parameters.description: Size of the module symbol, given before the module name.

parameters.name: 'module_name'
parameters.description: Module to create or instantiate.

parameters.name: 'prefix*'
parameters.description: Prefix for automatic instance names (the '*' marks it as prefix); without prefix or name the module name is used.

parameters.name: 'module_instance_name'
parameters.description: Explicit instance name (can be changed later with NAME).

parameters.name: +offset
parameters.description: Name parts by adding a multiple of 100 (see 'MODULE instance naming and offsets').

parameters.name: 'variant_name@module_name'
parameters.description: Use a specific assembly variant of the module.

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: R0, R90 ... as in ADD.

tools.notes: Mouse: center button mirrors, right rotates, Shift+Right rotates back. Board net names combine instance and net (MODULE1:N$1); a net exported through a PORT can be overridden by the net connected to that port. Edit the module symbol with MOVE; Ctrl+Left on its border resizes it. Related: PORT, EDIT name.mod, NAME, DESCRIPTION **.

tools.name: MODULE instance naming and offsets
tools.description: Parts of a module instance are named either in composite notation (instance:part, e.g. MODULE1:R17) or, with +offset, by adding the offset to the part number (R17 with offset 100 becomes R117). Offsets give short, familiar reference designators but must not collide with existing names.

parameters.name: +offset
parameters.description: Multiple of 100; each offset may be used only once in the schematic; only for instances on the main schematic level.

parameters.name: offset 0
parameters.description: Composite notation (instance:part).

tools.notes: EAGLE refuses an offset that would create existing names (e.g. offset 200 when R201..R209 already exist); choose large offsets to avoid confusion. Deeper hierarchy levels always use composite, path-like names (F0:SUB:C1). The instance properties dialog only offers unused offsets.

tools.name: MOVE
tools.description: Moves objects in any editor: click an object and click the target, or select it by name. Connected signal wires follow moved elements. Right click rotates and center click mirrors while moving, and Ctrl+right click takes the whole GROUP; click-and-drag moves immediately.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Part, pad, SMD, pin or gate name (full instance name for multi-gate parts); part attributes as R5>VALUE.
Special coordinate for the current mouse position, e.g. MOVE R1 (@).

parameters.name: Preserve Angles | Free | Disconnect (toolbar)
parameters.description: Keep wire angles (Ctrl snaps non-orthogonal wires to grid), follow the mouse freely, or detach the selection from its connections.

tools.notes: Mouse: Ctrl+Left selects at the origin/modifies (see 'MOVE with Ctrl'), Shift+Left takes a whole polygon, Ctrl+Right the group, Left&Drag / Ctrl+Right&Drag move immediately (no rotating then), center mirrors, right rotates, Shift+Right rotates back. Elements need tOrigins/bOrigins visible and cannot be moved when locked; invisible layers are not affected; wire ends attached to an element cannot be moved on their own. Shorts created by moving wires stay separate signals and are flagged by DRC. In schematics a Sup pin placed on a net names the net, pins placed on each other or unconnected pins placed on nets connect, but nets moved over pins do not. With 'Group default on', dragging a group member moves the group.

tools.name: MOVE group to another sheet
tools.description: Transfers part of a schematic sheet to another sheet without affecting the board: GROUP the objects, pick the group with MOVE, switch sheets while it hangs on the cursor, and place it. Parts take all their electrical connections along, so forward/back annotation stays consistent.
tools.usage:
GROUP •..
MOVE (> x y)
EDIT .sX
(x y)
tools.notes: The final (0 0) is the placement coordinate for the MOVE that is still active on the new sheet. Only wires with both ends in the group are transferred; a junction is added where a moved pin keeps a connection that would otherwise be invisible. Nothing happens if the target is the original sheet. To reorder sheets use EDIT .sX .sY.

tools.name: MOVE with Ctrl (snap, resize, bend)
tools.description: Holding Ctrl while selecting with MOVE changes what is moved: the selection point is pulled to the cursor and snapped to the current grid (useful for off-grid objects), a wire picked in the middle is bent into an arc, rectangles and circles are resized, and a port is moved alone. In scripts the C modifier in a coordinate, (C x y), simulates the Ctrl key.

parameters.name: object origin
parameters.description: Pulled to the cursor and snapped into the current grid.

parameters.name: wire middle
parameters.description: End points stay, the wire becomes an arc (or an arc's curvature changes).

parameters.name: rectangle corner / edge / center
parameters.description: Resize width and height / only width or height / snap the rectangle to grid.

parameters.name: circle circumference / center
parameters.description: Resize the diameter / snap the center to grid.

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: Moves only the port (affects all instances of the module).

tools.notes: Without Ctrl a selected object stays on the grid it was originally placed on. Shift+Left selects a polygon as a whole.
